The Mac (node 25e490e4) dispatched challenge session 01a1cf93-be8e-72a2-87a9-5cf0f86d75fc at 06:45:28 EST (h9kd.log: DraftChallengeEngine \\u0027challenge session ... dispatched\\u0027) and its verdict landed at 06:48 (publish as revised, 0 must, 1 should, 0 park; report ~/.hall9k/runs/01a1cf93-be8e-72a2-87a9-5cf0f86d75fc/challenge-report.md). The plan then applied a revision at 06:51 and published. At 08:10 a \\u0027challenge failed: another node dispatched it and recorded no outcome past the foreign-session ceiling\\u0027 entry was recorded against the same run and report, and the feed delivered \\u0027challenge ended with no verdict ... challenge again with h9k task challenge\\u0027 at 08:14. The Mac\\u0027s h9kd.log has no line for that failure, so another node of this owner recorded it. h9k task show 4bc02553 now shows Challenge \\u0027failed\\u0027 next to \\u0027Verdict on record ... the draft was revised since\\u0027. Harmless on a Done task, but on a live draft it would tell the operator to re-challenge (spending a session) a draft whose verdict exists, and plan drafts may hit the same. Find which condition the sweep reads as \\u0027no outcome\\u0027 (possibly the revision after the verdict, or the verdict event not reaching the other node before its ceiling) and make the sweep skip a challenge whose dispatching node recorded a verdict. A test that fails without the change covers the sweep on a challenge that has a verdict followed by a revision.\u0022,\u0022Constraints\u0022:null,\u0022ExternalReference\u0022:null,\u0022AddedAt\u0022:\u00222026-11-12T13:15:23.917367\u002B00:00\u0022,\u0022AddedByOwnerId\u0022:\u002201a00d41-5a50-7368-b048-72bcfee948bf\u0022,\u0022Model\u0022:\u0022\u0022,\u0022BlockedBy\u0022:[],\u0022StartsAsDraft\u0022:true,\u0022SourceIdeaId\u0022:null,\u0022EpicId\u0022:null,\u0022ReviewStageComposition\u0022:null,\u0022ReviewStageCompositionAcknowledged\u0022:false,\u0022StackedOnTaskId\u0022:null,\u0022PreApproved\u0022:false,\u0022Origin\u0022:null,\u0022PreApproval\u0022:\u0022Off\u0022,\u0022StackedOnPullRequestNumber\u0022:null,\u0022SecondaryExternalReference\u0022:null,\u0022SpikeKind\u0022:null,\u0022ExitCriterion\u0022:null,\u0022InitialScope\u0022:\u0022Fleet\u0022,\u0022HumanGate\u0022:false,\u0022EvolvedFromTaskId\u0022:null}","originEventId":"0cb50542-52e6-4c49-8669-7397f8f06a18","originSequence":183491,"originNodeId":"01a00d41-5b80-753d-a3f1-070b25e490e4","originOwnerRootFingerprint":"c8f5c85900dac9911ce1ada43484dc7bf91a2a3e86efa8812d9f84cfd25bf2ac","originAt":"2026-11-12T13:15:23.96329+00:00","originProjectId":"01a00d41-5d9a-73cc-b648-af431f721a71"},{"streamId":"01a1cfe6-1188-74e9-a49e-88dfe8516528","eventTypeName":"Hall9k.Domain.Features.Tasks.Events.DraftRefinementDispatched","eventDataJson":"{\u0022Id\u0022:\u002201a1cfe6-1188-74e9-a49e-88dfe8516528\u0022,\u0022SessionId\u0022:\u002201a1cfe6-32c1-7104-a5f4-b085e5a47d81\u0022,\u0022NodeId\u0022:\u002201a00d41-5b80-753d-a3f1-070b25e490e4\u0022,\u0022DispatchedAt\u0022:\u00222026-11-12T13:15:32.421773\u002B00:00\u0022,\u0022Model\u0022:\u0022claude-opus-5-5[1m]\u0022,\u0022Effort\u0022:\u0022high\u0022,\u0022Purpose\u0022:\u0022Refine\u0022}","originEventId":"7252977e-66b3-4750-9f72-d874c99c4bef","originSequence":183493,"originNodeId":"01a00d41-5b80-753d-a3f1-070b25e490e4","originOwnerRootFingerprint":"c8f5c85900dac9911ce1ada43484dc7bf91a2a3e86efa8812d9f84cfd25bf2ac","originAt":"2026-11-12T13:15:32.422788+00:00","originProjectId":"01a00d41-5d9a-73cc-b648-af431f721a71"},{"streamId":"01a1cfe6-1188-74e9-a49e-88dfe8516528","eventTypeName":"Hall9k.Domain.Features.Tasks.Events.TaskRevised","eventDataJson":"{\u0022Id\u0022:\u002201a1cfe6-1188-74e9-a49e-88dfe8516528\u0022,\u0022Objective\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:true,\u0022value\u0022:\u0022Another node\\u0027s foreign-session ceiling expiry never replaces a challenge or refinement outcome that the dispatching node recorded, and a node whose replication is behind does not record such an expiry on the first sweep that finds the dispatch overdue.\u0022},\u0022AcceptanceCriteria\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:true,\u0022value\u0022:[\u0022When a draft\\u0027s stream holds a challenge verdict for session S recorded by the node that dispatched S and also another node\\u0027s DispatchExpired failure for S, in either order, the verdict stays the draft\\u0027s latest challenge outcome in both TaskAggregate and TaskDetails: \\u0060h9k task show\\u0060 prints no failed challenge line for S, the publish gate reads the verdict, and a plan waiting on that challenge absorbs the verdict rather than the failure. A DB-free test applies dispatched S, the verdict, a revision, then the expiry (and separately dispatched S, the expiry, then the verdict) to both the aggregate and the projection, and the first ordering fails without the change.\u0022,\u0022The same holds for a refinement session R: when the dispatching node recorded an outcome for R and another node\\u0027s DispatchExpired for R is also on the stream, in either order, the dispatching node\\u0027s outcome is the latest refinement outcome, and the expiry leaves RevisedSinceLastDraftSession and RevisedWhileRefinementRan as the dispatching node\\u0027s outcome left them. A DB-free test covers both orderings on the aggregate and the projection.\u0022,\u0022A challenge outcome recorded for a session other than the running one, arriving while a later challenge session is running, changes neither the running session\\u0027s standing (its session id, node, dispatch time, model and effort) nor the latest challenge outcome, which is the guard refinement outcomes already have. A DB-free test fails without the change.\u0022,\u0022Neither DraftChallengeEngine nor PlanEngine ends another node\\u0027s dispatch on the first sweep that finds it past the foreign-session ceiling. It ends one only if the dispatch is still standing when a later sweep runs at least a settle period after the first, and the settle period is longer than the message sweep\\u0027s idle poll ceiling, so at least one replication read of the dispatching node\\u0027s outbox happens in between. An integration test per engine seeds an overdue foreign dispatch, runs a sweep that records nothing, appends the dispatching node\\u0027s outcome, runs a second sweep past the settle period, and finds no DispatchExpired on the stream. Without the change, the first sweep records one.\u0022,\u0022A dispatch from a node that never records an outcome is still ended once it has stood past the ceiling and stayed standing through the settle period. The existing tests for this, in DraftChallengeEngineTests and PlanEngineTests, still pass, changed only to account for the settle period.\u0022,\u0022docs/cli.md, where it says a dispatch another node made is ended past the foreign-session ceiling, also says the dispatch is ended only after the settle period and that the dispatching node\\u0027s own outcome wins over an expiry. If the settle period is a new daemon option, the options table in docs/operations.md has a row for it.\u0022]},\u0022AgentContext\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:true,\u0022value\u0022:\u0022## What happened\\n\\nOn 2026-11-12 one node dispatched a plan\\u0027s challenge session on a draft at 11:45:28 UTC, and in the same second the\\nrefinement session of a sibling draft. The challenge recorded a verdict at 11:48 and the refinement recorded Revised at\\n11:50. Both drafts were revised, published, and finished. At 13:10 UTC a second node of the same owner recorded\\nDispatchExpired for both sessions. Those records reached the first node at 13:14, and its feed told the operator to\\nchallenge again. \\u0060h9k task show\\u0060 on the first draft now prints a failed challenge beside the verdict, and on the sibling\\nit prints \\u0022Refinement not applied\\u0022 with the same reason. The first node had received nothing from the second between\\n11:23 and 13:14, and the expiries name sessions dispatched just before that silence began. The likely reading is that the\\nsecond node was suspended or offline from about 11:46, resumed at about 13:10, and swept before its inbox delivered\\noutcomes that had been recorded long before. That is inferred: the second node\\u0027s own store and log were not read.\\n\\nThe revision after the verdict is not the cause. Revisions only set RevisedWhileChallengeRan when a session is running\\n(\\u0060src/Hall9k.Domain/Features/Tasks/TaskAggregate.cs\\u0060, the \\u0060RevisedWhileChallengeRan |=\\u0060 line in the TaskRevised apply).\\nThe sweep reads TaskDetails.RunningChallengeSessionId, which a recorded outcome clears, so the expiring node had the\\ndispatch and not the outcome. The sweep can never skip a verdict it has not yet received, so the fix has two halves.\\n\\n## Where the code is (at a8cfd74dd)\\n\\n- The sweeps: \\u0060src/Hall9k.Daemon/Challenge/DraftChallengeEngine.cs\\u0060 \\u0060RecoverAsync\\u0060 (the \\u0060else if\\u0060 foreign branch) and\\n  \\u0060src/Hall9k.Daemon/Plan/PlanEngine.cs\\u0060 \\u0060RecoverAsync\\u0060 (the same branch for refinement). Both compare\\n  \\u0060DateTimeOffset.UtcNow - dispatchedAt\\u0060 against \\u0060_options.ForeignPublicationCeiling\\u0060. The expiry is recorded under the\\n  dispatching node\\u0027s id, so a receiver can tell an expiry only by its \\u0060Failure\\u0060 being \\u0060DispatchExpired\\u0060.\\n- The appliers: \\u0060TaskAggregate.Apply(DraftChallengeRecorded)\\u0060 and \\u0060Apply(DraftRefinementRecorded)\\u0060, and their\\n  counterparts in \\u0060src/Hall9k.Domain/Features/Tasks/Projections/TaskDetails.cs\\u0060. The refinement appliers already ignore\\n  an outcome for a session other than the running one, but not one that arrives after its own session\\u0027s outcome. The\\n  challenge appliers have neither guard.\\n- What reads the latest outcome: \\u0060ChallengeGate.Shortfall\\u0060, \\u0060PlanEngine\\u0060 (the loop that absorbs a challenge outcome\\n  whose \\u0060RecordedAt\\u0060 is at or after the plan\\u0027s request), and \\u0060TaskShowCommand\\u0060 (the challenge and refinement blocks).\\n- The message sweep\\u0027s idle cadence is \\u0060MessageIdlePollMinSeconds\\u0060 and \\u0060MessageIdlePollMaxSeconds\\u0060 in\\n  \\u0060src/Hall9k.Daemon/DaemonOptions.cs\\u0060. The replication read is \\u0060src/Hall9k.Daemon/Messaging/MessageSweepEngine.cs\\u0060.\\n\\n## The smallest shape\\n\\nOn the applier side, take one rule for both outcome types. An outcome for a session that is running applies, as today.\\nAn outcome for a session other than a running one is ignored. With nothing running, a DispatchExpired outcome for a\\nsession that already has an outcome is ignored, and a dispatching node\\u0027s outcome for a session whose latest outcome is\\nthat session\\u0027s own expiry replaces it. Any other outcome for a session that already has one is ignored. Outcomes with no\\nsession id (refused before a spawn) apply as today. That rule makes the end state the same whichever order the two\\nrecords arrive in, which matters because the expiring node itself receives the verdict after its own expiry.\\n\\nOn the sweep side, the smallest change is in-memory. Each engine remembers when it first saw each foreign session\\noverdue, ends the session only on a sweep at least the settle period later, and forgets sessions that are no longer\\nrunning. A restart starts the count over, which is the safe direction. One gap is accepted: a node suspended again\\nduring the settle period can expire on waking. The applier rule still corrects what every node shows, but the feed would\\ncarry the line. Making the sweep wait for an actual replication read of the dispatching node is the stronger fence, but\\nthat would couple the engines to the message sweep and cost more than the incident justifies.\\n\\nOut of scope: the publication session\\u0027s own foreign ceiling (the same option, a different engine), and changing the feed\\nso it describes events against stream state. Documents already projected with the stale failure keep it until\\nsomething rebuilds them; a rebuild is not required f721a71"},{"streamId":"01a1cfe6-1188-74e9-a49e-88dfe8516528","eventTypeName":"Hall9k.Domain.Features.Tasks.Events.DraftRefinementDispatched","eventDataJson":"{\u0022Id\u0022:\u002201a1cfe6-1188-74e9-a49e-88dfe8516528\u0022,\u0022SessionId\u0022:\u002201a1cff4-86a7-752f-8d43-a04c065af310\u0022,\u0022NodeId\u0022:\u002201a00d41-5b80-753d-a3f1-070b25e490e4\u0022,\u0022DispatchedAt\u0022:\u00222026-11-12T13:31:11.408372\u002B00:00\u0022,\u0022Model\u0022:\u0022claude-opus-5-5[1m]\u0022,\u0022Effort\u0022:\u0022high\u0022,\u0022Purpose\u0022:\u0022ApplyVerdict\u0022}","originEventId":"310236ce-fdb4-4e27-85dc-55d1cd1a37e5","originSequence":183586,"originNodeId":"01a00d41-5b80-753d-a3f1-070b25e490e4","originOwnerRootFingerprint":"c8f5c85900dac9911ce1ada43484dc7bf91a2a3e86efa8812d9f84cfd25bf2ac","originAt":"2026-11-12T13:31:11.409524+00:00","originProjectId":"01a00d41-5d9a-73cc-b648-af431f721a71"},{"streamId":"01a1cfe6-1188-74e9-a49e-88dfe8516528","eventTypeName":"Hall9k.Domain.Features.Tasks.Events.TaskRevised","eventDataJson":"{\u0022Id\u0022:\u002201a1cfe6-1188-74e9-a49e-88dfe8516528\u0022,\u0022Objective\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:false},\u0022AcceptanceCriteria\u0022:{\u0022hasValue\u0022:true,\u0022value\u0022:[\u0022When a draft\\u0027s stream holds challenge session S\\u0027s dispatch, a verdict for S recorded by the node that dispatched it, and another node\\u0027s DispatchExpired failure for S, in either order, TaskAggregate and TaskDetails end exactly as the same stream without the expiry would leave them. That covers the latest challenge outcome, the latest verdict, the running session\\u0027s standing, RevisedSinceChallengeVerdict, LatestChallengeVerdictJudgedOlderDraft, and RevisedSinceLastDraftSession. So \\u0060h9k task show\\u0060 prints no failed challenge line for S, and TaskDetails shows no challenge running with the verdict as the latest outcome, which is the fact the plan loop absorbs. The publish gate reads the verdict in both orderings; that part is a regression guard, because a failure already never replaces the latest verdict. A DB-free test applies the following to both the aggregate and the projection and compares each result against the same stream without the expiry: (a) dispatched S, a person\\u0027s revision, the verdict, a second revision, then the expiry; (b) dispatched S, a person\\u0027s revision, the expiry, then the verdict. Both orderings fail without the change.\u0022,\u0022The same holds for a refinement session R. When R\\u0027s dispatch, an outcome for R recorded by the node that dispatched it, and another node\\u0027s DispatchExpired failure for R are all on the stream, in either order, TaskAggregate and TaskDetails end exactly as the same stream without the expiry would leave them. That covers the latest refinement outcome, the running session\\u0027s standing, RevisedSinceLastDraftSession, RevisedWhileRefinementRan, and JudgedSinceChallengeVerdict. A DB-free test covers both orderings on the aggregate and the projection, each with a person\\u0027s revision made while R ran, and fails without the change.\u0022,\u0022A DispatchExpired failure recorded for a challenge or refinement session S changes nothing on the draft when it arrives after a later session T of the same kind was dispatched, whether T is still running or has already recorded its outcome. The same is true of the dispatching node\\u0027s own outcome for S when it arrives after T was dispatched on a node that had expired S. \\u0022Nothing\\u0022 covers T\\u0027s standing (session id, node, dispatch time, model and effort), the latest outcome, the latest verdict, ChallengeRequested, and the revision facts. A DB-free test covers both kinds, on the aggregate and the projection, with T running and with T recorded. The challenge cases, and the refinement cases with T already recorded, fail without the change.\u0022,\u0022Neither DraftChallengeEngine nor PlanEngine ends another node\\u0027s dispatch on the first sweep that finds it past the foreign-session ceiling. It ends one only if the dispatch is still standing when a later sweep of the same engine runs at least a settle period after the first. With default options the settle period is at least five minutes, so it spans several of the message sweep\\u0027s idle intervals (MessageIdlePollMaxSeconds), and a replication read that fails right after a node wakes still leaves later attempts inside the period. An integration test per engine does the following on one engine instance: seed an overdue foreign dispatch, run a sweep that records nothing, append the dispatching node\\u0027s outcome, run a second sweep after the settle period has passed, and find no DispatchExpired on the stream. Without the change, the first sweep records one.\u0022,\u0022A dispatch from a node that never records an outcome is still ended once it has stood past the ceiling and stayed standing through the settle period. The existing tests for this, Another_nodes_dispatch_stands_until_the_foreign_ceiling_and_is_then_ended_so_the_draft_can_be_challenged_again in DraftChallengeEngineTests and Another_nodes_refinement_dispatch_stands_until_the_foreign_ceiling_and_is_then_ended_on_the_task in PlanEngineTests, still pass, changed only to run both sweeps on one engine instance and to account for the settle period.\u0022,\u0022docs/cli.md, where it says a dispatch another node made is ended past the foreign-session ceiling, also says the dispatch is ended only after the settle period and that the dispatching node\\u0027s own outcome wins over an expiry.
